anomalies.observed: J8 is a two-pin connector/header whose pin 1 is on NET0053 and whose pin 2 is on NET0056. NET0053 contains the battery negative/return path (U3.2 and barrel-jack switch pin J9.3), while NET0056 is the BAT+ rail (U1 cathode, J7 USB VBUS, J9 barrel center, IC2 VIN/EN, C4, and J8.2).
anomalies.expected: The positive battery/adapter rail and the battery negative/return rail must not be directly bridged by a header or jumper. The specification describes BAT- as reaching only the battery holder and the barrel-jack switch contact; no intended component should connect BAT- to BAT+.

evidence.quote: BAT- only otherwise reaches U7.2 and J6.1

anomalies.impact: If a jumper or wire is installed on J8, the 18650 cell and the BAT+ input rail are shorted to the battery negative/return. This would cause a hard short, rapid battery discharge, possible damage to the battery, barrel jack, USB input, and regulator, and would prevent normal power operation.

anomalies.observed: C6 is declared as a 0.1 uF capacitor (libsource Device C) but is assigned an inductor footprint, Inductor_SMD:L_0805_2012Metric_Pad1.05x1.20mm_HandSolder. Its pin 2 is connected to GND, while pin 1 is in an unconnected net.
anomalies.expected: A capacitor should use a capacitor footprint and, if intended as a bypass/decoupling part, should connect from a supply rail to GND. A floating capacitor in an inductor footprint is a design/assembly identity error and should either be corrected or removed.
anomalies.impact: The part may be misidentified or misassembled, and as wired it provides no bypass function. If it was intended as a decoupling capacitor, the missing connection could leave the associated rail less well filtered; if it is not needed, it is an extraneous floating part.
